detailed_analysis: The spectrum is diagnostic of a CaCO3-family carbonate. The four internal/external mode groups match the carbonate fingerprint: (1) ν1 symmetric CO3 stretch at 1085.2 cm-1 (dominant, sharp, FWHM ~2.7 cm-1); (2) ν4 in-plane bend resolved as a doublet at 701.3 and 705.7 cm-1; (3) lattice/external modes at ~156, 190, 213, 272, and 284 cm-1; and (4) broad higher-shift bands at 1206 and 1238 cm-1 (likely combination/overtone or ν3-region features). The critical discriminator is polymorph identity. Per the mandatory domain rules, calcite shows ν1 ~1086 with a SINGLE ν4 near 712 and a lattice mode near 282, whereas aragonite shows ν1 ~1085 with a ν4 DOUBLET at 705+701 and lattice modes near 152 and 206. The fitted spectrum has a clearly resolved 701/706 ν4 doublet plus the ~156/213 lattice pattern, which matches ARAGONITE and rules against calcite (a single 712 band and 282 mode are not what is observed). The resolved ν4 doublet is the decisive feature and exactly the polymorph separator the rules emphasize. The ν1 core/wing decomposition (1085.2 sharp core + 1083.0 broader wing) is a fitting device rather than two physical modes; the residual ringing at the apex most plausibly reflects finite spectrometer sampling of an extremely narrow line, slight instrumental asymmetry, or minor detector nonlinearity at very high count rates, rather than a distinct vibrational transition. Band summary (center cm-1, relative intensity, strongest first): 1085.2 (1.00), 701.3 (0.15), 213.4 (0.09), 705.7 (0.10), 189.5 (0.06), 1238.1 (0.07), 272.0 (0.03), 283.7 (0.03), 1206.3 (0.05), 142.8 (0.02), 156.0 (0.005), 1105 (0.02). Note: relative intensities use fitted amplitudes; the 1083/1085 pair should be summed as one ν1. No sample chemistry (EDX/XRF) was provided, so this identification is pattern-only; the pattern is internally consistent with aragonite but Ca is not independently confirmed.

scientific_claims.claim: The sample is identified as aragonite (CaCO3 orthorhombic polymorph) on the basis of a resolved ν4 doublet at 701.3 ± 0.02 and 705.7 ± 0.02 cm-1 together with ν1 at 1085.2 ± 0.003 cm-1 and lattice modes at ~156 and ~213 cm-1, distinguishing it from calcite.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: Polymorph discrimination between aragonite and calcite is central to biomineralization, paleoclimate proxies, and diagenesis studies; the ν4 doublet and low-frequency lattice modes provide the definitive Raman signature and prevent the common misassignment of aragonite as calcite from the ν1 band alone.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone confirmed that a resolved Raman ν4 doublet near 701/706 cm-1 with ν1 at ~1085 cm-1 uniquely identifies aragonite versus calcite in unknown CaCO3 samples?

model_type: Sum of 13 pseudo-Voigt profiles on a linear baseline (nu1 core/wing split, nu4 doublet, lattice modes, high-x doublet)

verification_iterations.model: Sum of pseudo-Voigt profiles on a linear baseline. 9 components: (1) ~185 cm⁻¹ lattice mode, (2) ~213 cm⁻¹ lattice mode, (3) ~272 cm⁻¹ and (4) ~284 cm⁻¹ (resolved doublet from zoom), (5) ~700 cm⁻¹ and (6) ~706 cm⁻¹ (ν4 doublet from zoom), (7) ~1088 cm⁻¹ strong ν1 symmetric stretch, (8) ~1100 cm⁻¹ shoulder, (9) ~1210 cm⁻¹ and add ~1240 cm⁻¹ — the high-wavenumber region is a doublet, so 10 components total (splitting 9 into 1210 + 1240).

issues.problem: The dominant peak is systematically under-fit at its apex and its width/shape is wrong. The fit peaks at ~20000 while data reaches ~22000, and the fit is too narrow on the rising/falling flanks, producing a large dispersive (derivative-like) residual with 4 sign-changes.

Multiple real features are unmodelled/under-resolved. The data shows a clear shoulder near ~142.8 and a peak near ~161 that the fit renders as essentially zero baseline, and the peak near ~189 is under-fit.
The sharp doublet apexes are under-resolved; the fit undershoots both maxima (~701 and ~706) and produces a ringing residual.
Localized systematic residual with 5 sign-changes indicates the ~1207/~1238 doublet shape is not fully captured.

verification_iterations.fix_applied: Add components seeded at x≈1085 (narrow core on the main peak), x≈142.8, and x≈161; free/relax peak-shape (eta) and widths on peaks 5/6 and the main peak, then refit.

verification_iterations.model: Sum of pseudo-Voigt profiles on a linear baseline, now 13 components: (1) ~142.8 cm⁻¹ lattice shoulder (NEW), (2) ~161 cm⁻¹ weak lattice mode (NEW), (3) ~189 cm⁻¹ lattice mode (re-seeded/broadened from prior ~185), (4) ~213 cm⁻¹ lattice mode, (5) ~272 cm⁻¹ and (6) ~284 cm⁻¹ resolved lattice doublet, (7) ~701 cm⁻¹ and (8) ~706 cm⁻¹ ν4 bending doublet (widths/eta freed), (9) ~1085 cm⁻¹ SHARP CORE of the ν1 symmetric stretch and (10) ~1088 cm⁻¹ BROADER WING sharing the ν1 apex (core/wing two-component decomposition, replacing the single dominant band), (11) ~1100 cm⁻¹ shoulder, (12) ~1207 cm⁻¹ and (13) ~1238 cm⁻¹ high-wavenumber doublet. This is consistent with a sulfate/carbonate-like species: strong ν1 symmetric stretch near 1085 (with a sharp lorentzian-dominated core on broader wings), ν4 bending doublet near 700, and lattice/external modes below ~300 cm⁻¹. The core/wing split on ν1 is justified by the derivative-like residual with 4 sign-changes and the apex under-fit (fit 20000 vs data 22000), which a single symmetric profile cannot reproduce.

issues.problem: Sharp derivative-like residual at the apex of the dominant peak (±500 counts, ringing with 4 sign-changes).
Low-amplitude wavy residual (±100 on features up to ~1900).
